what_happened: Seed report's design question 1 hoped gate-cache-lib.sh's corpus-digest machinery could supply a touched-path diff for free; traced gate_cache_entry_write/read and confirmed the persisted cache entry stores only one opaque composite hash per gate, never per-file hashes -- there is nothing to diff. Had to fall back to the orchestrator's existing invocation_modified_files as the only real touched-path source, which lives outside this task's declared file_scope.

Mechanically traced a concrete cache-correctness risk: verify-deploy.sh's generic --skip-unchanged cache-write block (~line 2251) writes a cache entry for a gate whenever it ran clean, keyed by the gate's DECLARED corpus (whole @extensions tree for gate 8), with no awareness of whether gate8_run internally narrowed its own run-all.sh invocation via --only. If gate 8 is wired to narrow without a companion fix, a narrowed-but-clean pass would wrongly certify the full corpus as green, letting a later --skip-unchanged run skip gate 8 entirely. Recommended forcing GATE_DIRTY_LIST membership whenever gate8_run narrows, regardless of outcome, as a precondition for shipping the narrowing at all.

Seed report's '149 suites' figure (measured 2026-11-10) had drifted to 195 by 2026-11-16 (confirmed via a precise find-based per-extension tally matching run-all.sh's own discovery loop exactly). The 17-gate @extensions set and gate8's 662,462ms cost were unchanged.

Dispatch description's '17 of 28 gates declare @extensions' denominator has drifted: the live gate-registry.data now holds 29 gates. The 17-gate id set itself re-derived exactly as stated, and the 'all 149 suites' figure is 195 live (research report 02 had already corrected it). Corrections recorded in the plan's Carried-Figure Re-Validation table.

Research report 02 had already traced the generic --skip-unchanged cache-write hazard to a specific code path and ruled out the gate cache as a touched-path source, so planning needed no re-investigation of either; the plan phases map almost one-to-one onto its recommendations. Plan validated clean (0 warnings) on first validate-artifact.sh run, including the Tier Justification measurement check.

Plan Phase 1 task said to declare GATE8_TOUCHED's default beside GATE8_JOBS (which sits AFTER the argument-parsing while loop). Doing so literally clobbers the value --gate8-touched's case arm sets inside that loop, since the post-loop default assignment runs later and overwrites it back to empty. Fixed by declaring GATE8_TOUCHED="" before the while loop instead (alongside GATES_FILTER/JOBS), matching the actual execution order; GATE8_JOBS has no case arm so its own post-loop placement is fine and unaffected.

gate8_run()'s unnarrowed run-all.sh invocation used "${GATE8_ONLY_ARGS[@]:-}" to expand a possibly-empty array. Direct reproduction confirmed that under set -uo pipefail (bash 5.3.9), the :- default form substitutes ONE empty-string WORD for a declared-but-zero-element array (argc=1), unlike the bare [@] form which correctly expands to zero words (argc=0). This caused every unnarrowed (absent-flag or sentinel-fallback) gate8 run to pass a spurious empty argument to run-all.sh, which rejected it with 'ERROR: unknown argument: ' and exit 2 -- a real regression in the absent-flag byte-identical-output guarantee, caught only by actually running the gate (not by code review or bash -n/shellcheck). Fixed by using the bare "${GATE8_ONLY_ARGS[@]}" (no default) for the argument-list expansion; this file's pre-existing GATE_RAN_LIST/GATE_DIRTY_LIST [@]:- reads elsewhere are unaffected since they are for-loop iterands where one spurious empty string is harmless -- that idiom must never be copied into an argument-list expansion.

A full-battery (unnarrowed) --only-gate 8 run against the live repo intermittently exits 1 right now (observed: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh's documented load-sensitivity, and/or test-gate-lock.sh's own nested fixtures inheriting the real GATE_MUTEX_HELD=1 that a genuinely-top-level gate8_run() exports to its run-all.sh child and that child's own suite-fixture descendants). Confirmed this is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to task 584's Phase 2 changes: ran the byte-identical, completely unmodified deployed .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh (zero --gate8-touched references, predates this task) under the identical --skip-unchanged --only-gate 8 invocation and observed the identical exit-1/FAIL output. Phase 2's own narrowed-path behavior (the only new code) was verified cleanly and directly: narrowing, sentinel fallback, and the forced cache-ineligibility invariant (Case E) all confirmed correct via small, targeted suite subsets that avoid this flaky full-battery path.

Phase 3's new test-gate8-suite-selection.sh file was not declared in agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json's provides.scripts list, which doc-lint (check-extension-docs.sh) caught as 'script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts'. Without this declaration deploy-headless.sh would never deploy the new suite file. Added the one-line entry (alphabetically after test-gate8-expected-new-distinction.sh). manifest.json is not in this task's declared file_scope -- this is a legitimate, minimal out-of-scope touch required for the new suite to actually ship, not a scope-creep edit.
